summary: Serbia's Statistical Office publishes convicted adults by self-declared national affiliation (Serb, Hungarian, Roma and others) for every chapter of the Criminal Code. That is real ethnicity data for perpetrators, but only by broad chapter, never by child-specific offence, and unknown for almost half. Victims are published by age and sex only; trafficking victims are listed by country of origin.

nations.Republic of Serbia (excl. Kosovo and Met: RZS court-based perpetrator statistics; trafficking victim centre.

european_title: Serbs are separately identified; ethnic Europeans as a whole are not a category
european_note: RZS records national affiliation (Serb, Montenegrin, Albanian, Hungarian, Muslim, Roma, Romanian, other). Serbs, the largest European group, are shown separately, but the published 'other' column mixes European and non-European groups, so ethnic Europeans as a whole cannot be computed. It covers convicted adults only, by offence chapter.

harms.label: Offences against sexual freedom (convicted adults, all victim ages)
harms.intro: 272 adults were convicted of offences against sexual freedom in 2024. Courts recorded a national affiliation for 144 of them: 140 Serbs, 3 Roma and 1 other; for 128 (47%) it was not declared or not known. The chapter includes sexual intercourse with a child (17 convicted) and mixes child and adult victims: of 262 victims with data, 149 were under 18. Victims have no nationality.

victims.text: RZS Table 3.11 gives victims' sex and age for each offence, but no nationality, ethnicity or citizenship.

perpetrators.scope: Serbia, adults convicted of offences against sexual freedom (all victim ages), 2024
perpetrators.n_label: convicted adults with a declared national affiliation (of 272)
perpetrators.rate_reason: Not published; no population denominators by national affiliation are given with the crime data.
perpetrators.share_note: RZS Bulletin 725, Table 3.6 (2024). Counts: Serbs 140, Hungarians 0, Roma 3, other declared 1, not declared 1, not known 127. Of 262 victims with data, 72 were under 14 and 77 aged 14-17. National affiliation (nacionalna pripadnost) is the convicted person's self-declared ethnic or national group, recorded by the court on the RZS SK-2 form. It is real ethnicity data, not citizenship. 'Other declared' combines Montenegrins, Albanians, Muslims (as an ethnic group), Romanians and all other groups. Unknown combines 'not declared' (no one is obliged to declare) and 'not known' (not recorded). Shares are of people whose affiliation is known. Excludes Kosovo and Metohija.

breakdown.why: RZS Bulletin 725 (2024 data) gives adults convicted of offences against sexual freedom (272) by self-declared national affiliation: 140 Serbs, 3 Roma, 1 other; affiliation not known or not declared for 128 (47%). The chapter mixes child and adult victims (149 of 262 victims with data were under 18); victims have age and sex but no nationality. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Adults convicted of offences against marriage and family (3,209; includes domestic violence and neglect and abuse of a minor) by national affiliation: 1,546 Serbs, 34 Roma, 6 Hungarians, 28 other; 1,595 (50%) not known or not declared. All victim ages; no victim nationality. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Adults convicted of offences against life and body (1,313; murders plus bodily injury) by national affiliation: 707 Serbs, 12 Roma, 4 Hungarians, 20 other; 570 (43%) not known or not declared. All victim ages; murder victims have age (4 of 96 under 14) but no nationality. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

The Centre for Protection of Victims of Trafficking identified 75 victims in 2025 (41% children) and lists them by country of origin (47 Serbia, 28 foreign), not by age and citizenship together. Convicted traffickers (11 in 2024, with 17 victims, 5 of them children) appear by national affiliation only within the crimes-against-humanity chapter (22 convicted, 16 unknown or not declared). Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Child pornography offences (Art. 185: 26 convicted, 17 child victims) are inside the sexual-freedom chapter, published by national affiliation only as a whole (47% unknown or not declared). No victim nationality. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm. Heritage points require that link as a published cross-table for the same child cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points and is awarded only for a published cross-table that records child victim heritage and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage. Coverage is 10, rates 7.5 and access 7.5. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points, and only when that pair is published. A published “White” category that merges Hispanic people or another group, so ethnic Europeans cannot be isolated, is scored as a proxy under the same cap. A country with no real ethnicity data is capped at 25%. Neglect is not part of the score.
score.why: Serbia scores 9% on the stricter scale (0-20%). Heritage points are 0 because there is no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data earns no heritage credit. It is the only batch-5 country with real ethnicity data: courts record convicted adults' self-declared national affiliation (Serb, Roma, Hungarian and others) and the Statistical Office publishes it for every chapter of the Criminal Code, so the 25% cap does not apply. Points stay low because it covers perpetrators only, by broad chapter rather than child-specific offence, with 47% unknown or not declared, and victims have no nationality at all.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 24 Nov 2026 (homicide 27.78, sexual abuse 22.22, sex trafficking 22.22, physical abuse 16.67, online exploitation 11.11); paired-data rule: heritage points only for a published child victim×offender cross-table

paired_child.basis: No published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.

rzs_b.name: Bilten 725: Punoletni učinioci krivičnih dela u Republici Srbiji, 2024
rzs_b.publisher: Republički zavod za statistiku (Statistical Office of the Republic of Serbia)
rzs_b.records: Reported, accused and convicted adults by offence; convicted adults by national affiliation (Table 3.6) and citizenship (Table 3.10); victims by sex and age per offence (Table 3.11).
rzs_b.limitations: National affiliation is published by offence chapter only, for convicted adults only, and is not declared or not known for 47%. Victims have no nationality. Excludes Kosovo and Metohija.

rzs_r.name: Saopštenje SK12 br. 180: Punoletni učinioci krivičnih dela, 2025
rzs_r.records: 69,641 adults reported, 25,866 accused and 22,498 convicted in 2025, by offence group, sex and age.
rzs_r.limitations: No national affiliation or citizenship in the release; those appear in the December bulletin.

cztlj.name: Statistički izveštaj Centra za zaštitu žrtava trgovine ljudima za 2025. godinu
cztlj.publisher: Centar za zaštitu žrtava trgovine ljudima (Centre for Protection of Victims of Trafficking, a state institution)
cztlj.records: 242 reports, 75 formally identified victims (41% children) by sex, age, form of exploitation, country of origin and country of exploitation.
cztlj.limitations: Scanned PDF; country of origin is not split by age; no trafficker data.

rzsz.name: Deca u sistemu socijalne zaštite 2024; Izveštaj o zaštiti dece od dečijih brakova 2024
rzsz.publisher: Republički zavod za socijalnu zaštitu (Republic Institute for Social Protection)
rzsz.records: Reports of violence against children by type, sex and age; the child-marriage report gives national affiliation of child victims (117 of 177 Roma).
rzsz.limitations: No ethnicity for child victims of physical, sexual or emotional violence or neglect. Child marriage is not one of the five scored harms.

availability_note: Each harm has an 'availability' map listing the victim and perpetrator groups with any published figure (overall and by measure) and any linked victim-perpetrator pairs. Groups not listed have no data for that harm; the explorer should grey them out rather than offer an empty combination.
